title: Lighting — User Manual
summary: Control Shelly, Tasmota, and any HTTP-controllable lighting/IoT device locally, plus how to use LAN Discover.

sections.body:
Overview

Lighting controls smart switches and dimmable lights directly over the local network — no cloud account required for any device. It isn't tied to one vendor: a pluggable driver system supports Shelly and Tasmota firmware natively, plus a Generic HTTP driver that can front almost anything else with a web-controllable endpoint (Home Assistant automations, ESPHome, IFTTT/webhook proxies, self-built relays).

Key Features

  • Multi-protocol devices — each device has a Device Type of Shelly, Tasmota, or Generic HTTP, chosen once at creation and not editable afterward (the fields it stores differ by type).

  • Shelly & Tasmota — addressed by IP (and optional port); generation/switch-vs-light detection happens automatically on first contact and again whenever a card refreshes.

  • Generic HTTP — addressed entirely by URLs you supply: an On URL and Off URL (required), plus an optional Status URL and a dot-notation Status JSON Path (e.g. state.on) if the device can report its own state.

  • Discover — sweeps a /24 subnet (enter the first three octets; the last octet is scanned .1–.254) looking for Shelly and Tasmota devices, the same way the Network Topology Map's IP Range Scanner works. Found devices can be added individually or all at once via Adopt All. Generic HTTP devices have no fixed signal to scan for, so they're always added manually.

  • Live status — every card auto-refreshes every 10 seconds (or on demand via Refresh Now), showing Online/Offline and, where the driver supports it, live power draw (W).

  • Power & brightness control — a toggle switch on every card; a brightness slider appears for devices detected as dimmable lights (never for Generic HTTP, which has no brightness protocol). Dragging the slider only sends the command on release, not on every pixel of movement.

Step-by-Step

  1. To add a device you already know the address for, click Add Device, choose its Device Type, and fill in either the IP Address/Port (Shelly/Tasmota) or the On/Off/Status URLs (Generic HTTP).

  2. To find Shelly/Tasmota devices on your network instead, use the Discover panel: enter the first three octets of your subnet and click Scan Network. Watch the progress bar, then click Add next to a result or Adopt All to add every result at once.

  3. Once added, use the Power toggle on a device's card to switch it on/off, and the brightness slider (if present) to dim it.

  4. Click the edit icon to rename a device, move it to a different Location, or change its connection details (Generic HTTP URLs, or IP/Port for Shelly/Tasmota).

  5. Click the trash icon to remove a device from Lighting entirely.

Tips

  • If a device shows "detecting..." for its kind, it hasn't answered a probe yet — check that it's powered on and reachable; the next auto-refresh (every 10s) will try again.

  • For a Generic HTTP device with no Status URL configured, the card simply won't update its on/off state from polling — it keeps showing whatever the last successful Power command set, since there's nothing to read.

  • Cloud-only ecosystems (Hue, LIFX, Govee, Tuya) aren't supported as dedicated drivers — they require OAuth/cloud API keys, a different integration shape from this module's local-first design. If you have a bridge or automation that exposes a plain HTTP endpoint for one of those, add it as a Generic HTTP device instead.
